title: Diagnose, price and lead: improving a distributed team
course_title: Remote Work & Team Collaboration: Leading Distributed Teams

say: Diagnose, price and lead: improving a distributed team.
This is the video for module three of Remote Work and Team Collaboration.
Whether you join a remote team, lead it, or advise it, your first job is to understand how work really flows. Teams often describe the way they wish they worked.

panel.heading: Find how the team really works
items: Teams describe how they wish they worked

say: So ask for evidence, not just opinions. Where is the current budget? Show me.

say: Talk to people at different levels and locations, including someone who joined recently. Keep what they say confidential, and report patterns, not names.

say: Score eight areas, such as channels, source of truth, ownership, meetings and decisions. A score of 1 means no shared practice.

panel.heading: Score eight areas from 1 to 5
items: 5: written, and most people follow it
Add the scores; find the lowest areas

say: 3 means a practice exists but is used unevenly. 5 means a written practice that most people follow.

say: For example, Grace reviewed a volunteer network and scored 17 out of 40. It took 11 minutes and three people to find the current volunteer list, and two versions disagreed by 23 names.

say: Do not try to fix everything. Place each fix by how much it helps against how hard it is.
Start with quick wins. For Grace, a decision log and one master volunteer list take a few hours each.

cards.d: High impact, low effort. For Grace: a shared decision log and one master volunteer list.
High impact, high effort. For Grace: a full handbook, next quarter.
Low value and costly. For Grace: buying a paid tool, because the problem is habit.

say: Plan the big projects carefully, like a full handbook for the following quarter.

say: Turn each recommendation into a deliverable that can be checked, then price it as a day rate times estimated days.
Bimpe aims for 800,000 naira a month and expects to bill about 10 days, so her day rate is 80,000 naira.

card.title: Pricing a 10-day project
card.note: Illustrative naira figures, not market rates.

say: She estimates 10 days of work, which gives a base of 800,000 naira. She adds 10 percent for unknowns, 80,000 naira.

card.title: Pricing a 10-day project
card.note: Illustrative naira figures, not market rates.

say: Her fixed price is 880,000 naira. Half is paid on signing, and half when the deliverables are accepted.
She also writes what is out of scope, like buying paid software. These figures are illustrative, not market rates.

say: Scope creep often arrives as a casual WhatsApp message: while you are at it, can you also set up the board for finance? Do not refuse, and do not silently agree. Send a short change request.

panel.heading: When an extra request arrives
items: State the effect on the timeline
Ask the approver to accept in writing

say: Describe the request, and estimate the cost. For example, 2 extra days times 80,000 is 160,000 naira.

say: Say how the timeline moves, and ask the named approver to accept in writing. An email reply is enough.

say: Protect the money too. Confirm bank details by phone with a known contact before any transfer.
Be suspicious of sudden new account instructions by email or WhatsApp. It is a common fraud pattern.
If you are registered with the CAC, invoice in that name. And keep the client's written acceptance as your record.

panel.heading: Payments and fraud
items: Confirm bank details by phone first
Invoice in your registered business name

say: Leaders are trusted when their own work is reliable and visible. Every time you say I will, add it to one list within the hour, with a date.

panel.heading: Capture, plan, do, review
items: Capture every I will within the hour

say: On Monday choose the three most important outcomes, and block focus time for them.

panel.heading: Capture, plan, do, review
items: Capture every I will within the hour

say: Post a short start-of-day and end-of-day line. On Friday, check every commitment and renegotiate early.
Uche tracked 14 commitments and found her one late item was promised on a call and never captured. Now she writes it down after every call.

panel.heading: Capture, plan, do, review

say: To remember. Diagnose with evidence and score eight areas. Fix quick wins first.
Price from a day rate and estimated days, with a stated contingency and clear payment terms.
Handle extra requests in writing. And keep your own promises visible, renegotiating early instead of missing silently.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Ask for evidence, score eight areas
Quick wins first; state your limits
Price: day rate x days, plus contingency
Change requests in writing before extra work
